issues.legal_issue: A conviction for bribery and conspiracy cannot be sustained on circumstantial evidence when the circumstances relied on are materially contradicted or not firmly established as pointing to guilt.
material_facts: The prosecution relied on the accused referring the complainant to a colleague, but that conduct was also compatible with an innocent explanation.
The complainant’s testimony about a later conversation with the accused was materially contradicted in cross-examination.
The alleged presence of the accused during a colleague’s reduced bribe demand was contradicted by the complainant’s own testimony and was inconsistent with the official charge-transfer record.
The accused was absent when the colleague accepted the tainted money, and the evidence did not reliably establish the accused’s participation in the demand or an agreement to share the money.
issues.conclusion: The circumstantial evidence was too infirm to safely support the convictions; the appeal was allowed and the convictions and sentences were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Where a prosecution rests on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances must first be firmly established and must be a definite pointer towards the accused’s guilt. Material contradictions and unproved circumstances make it unsafe to convict. The charges involved Section 5(1)(d) and Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, and Sections 161 and 120B read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this principle.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed against a criminal conviction.
predicates.circumstantial_evidence_case: The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence to establish the accused’s guilt.
predicates.essential_circumstances_materially_contr: Material circumstances relied on by the prosecution were contradicted or were not firmly established.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction based on circumstantial evidence and material circumstances are contradicted or unproved, the conviction and sentence are set aside.
